name: 80円焼鳥 信長 水道橋店 (80-Yen Yakitori Nobunaga, Suidobashi Branch)

claims.text: Yakitori tare (basting glaze) at Japanese yakitori restaurants is standardly soy-sauce based and therefore typically contains wheat; no gluten-free/tamari alternative was mentioned for this restaurant in any source found.

name: アイスの沼 浅草 伝法院通り店 (Aisu no Numa Asakusa Denboin-dori)

claims.text: No source addresses cross-contamination practices for this shop; gelato is typically scooped from open cases with shared scoops, a common cross-contact concern for celiac customers, but this shop's specific handling is unconfirmed.
No source confirms whether dairy-based and any non-dairy/fruit-based flavors are scooped with separate equipment.

name: 網焼きジンギスカン 羊肉酒場 悟大 水道橋店 (Amiyaki Jingisukan Yōniku Sakaba Godai — Sui)

claims.text: No specific cross-contamination information was published; meat is grilled directly on open-flame nets shared across orders, which is a plausible cross-contact pathway for allergen-sensitive diners though not explicitly documented.
Jingisukan is conventionally served with a soy-sauce-based tare dipping sauce; standard Japanese soy sauce contains wheat. No wheat-free tare or soy sauce alternative was confirmed for this location.

name: Bistro Beppinsha (カリー＆ワイン ビストロべっぴん舎 お茶の水本店)

claims.text: Shared 14-seat curry-and-wine bistro kitchen with no advertised celiac/allergy protocol; wheat items (wine-bistro sides, bread) may be handled nearby.

Japanese gluten-free authority explains most soy sauce contains wheat and is not gluten-free; only tamari/isiru substitutes are safe — i.e. a Japanese dish can be '小麦粉不使用' yet still contain wheat via soy sauce, so Beppinsha's flour-free claim does not establish celiac safety.
claims.source: https://glutenfree.co.jp/blog/醤油はグルテンフリーなの？/diary/

claims.text: Beppinsha's GF descriptor is only the shop's own marketing copy repeated by tourism/food blogs (『小麦粉を使わないグルテンフリーのカリー』); no celiac review, no allergen protocol, and no ingredient disclosure for soy sauce/Worcester in the broth was found in any source.

The documented lunch set includes rice, potato salad, pickled onions and coffee — the potato salad is mayonnaise/egg based and neither its nor the pickles' wheat/allergen content is disclosed, undercutting a blanket 'options' GF and any vegan reading.

No FindMeGlutenFree or HappyCow celiac review of Beppinsha Ochanomizu could be located; the only GF-in-Tokyo result was a generic travel guide — i.e. the required independent corroboration does not exist.

A Beppinsha Jimbocho branch is flagged '[Closed]' on Tabelog, signaling operational churn across the brand; the Ochanomizu main store's current status/menu could not be re-verified because Tabelog and the official site both returned HTTP 403.
Not documented whether any component uses wheat-based soy or Worcestershire sauce; the curry broth itself is stated to be flour-free but seasoning details are unverified — confirm with staff.
Curries contain meat/seafood and the set includes mayonnaise-based potato salad; no vegan preparation documented.
No celiac allergy-handling procedure is published; GF is a product characteristic (wheat-free curry) rather than a managed protocol.
Shop explicitly states 「小麦粉を使わないグルテンフリーカリー」 — the signature curries are made without wheat flour and use spices, not roux, to thicken.
「小麦粉を使わないさらさらの薬膳カレー」 — a thin, roux-free medicinal broth, reducing the classic wheat-flour risk of Japanese curry.

name: 豚ノヴァ零-zero- 神田水道橋店 (Butanova Zero Kanda-Suidobashi)

claims.text: Standard Jiro-style tare/soy-based seasoning is used; no wheat-free alternative or gluten information is published for this shop.
Shio (salt) and tare (sauce) skewers are cooked on the same shared charcoal grill; no separation between wheat-sauce-glazed and plain items is documented.
The tare glazing sauce used on charcoal-grilled yakitori is, per standard preparation, soy-sauce based and therefore contains wheat; no gluten-free tare alternative is documented for this shop.
Any vegetable skewers would be grilled on the same charcoal grill used for chicken, quail, and pigeon.
Sukiyaki at Chinya is cooked in a traditional warishita (sweetened soy-sauce sauce); standard Japanese soy sauce is brewed with wheat, and no wheat-free or tamari-based alternative is advertised.

The core dish is built around wagyu beef cooked in a shared pot with a soy-based sauce and finished with a raw-egg dip, so there is no realistic way to keep a vegan order separate from meat-based cooking.

name: 中華菜房 達磨 (Chuka Saibo Daruma)

claims.text: Standard Japanese-style soy sauce (containing wheat) appears to be used throughout the menu, as is typical for machi-chuka cooking; no wheat-free soy sauce alternative was found in any source.
